chapterTag.category: AP Calc BC BC-2 — Logistic & Euler's Method

body.en: BC adds a richer population model and a numerical method for approximating solutions to differential equations.
Logistic: \( \dfrac{dP}{dt}=kP\!\left(1-\dfrac{P}{M}\right) \), carrying capacity \( M \), fastest growth at \( P=\tfrac{M}{2} \). Euler's method steps forward: \( y_{n+1}=y_n+h\,f(x_n,y_n) \).

figure.title: Logistic Growth Curve: Carrying Capacity and Inflection Point

caption.en: Logistic growth curve $P(t) = \frac{10}{1 + 9e^{-0.9t}}$ with carrying capacity $M=10$. Growth is fastest at the inflection point where $P = M/2 = 5$ and $\frac{d^2P}{dt^2} = 0$. The curve is concave up on $(0, 2.44)$ and concave down on $(2.44, \infty)$.

label.en: ⚠️ AP Exam Traps: Logistic Models & Euler's Method

body.en:
• Fastest Growth is at Population \( P = M/2 \), NOT Time \( t = M/2 \): When the exam asks 'for what population is the growth rate greatest?', the answer is always half the carrying capacity \( M/2 \). If it asks 'at what time is the growth rate greatest?', substitute \( P = M/2 \) into the particular solution and solve for \( t \).
  • Factoring Non-Standard Logistic Forms: If given \( \frac{dP}{dt} = 0.2P - 0.0005P^2 \), factor out \( 0.2P \): \( 0.2P\left(1 - \frac{0.0005}{0.2}P\right) = 0.2P\left(1 - \frac{P}{400}\right) \). The carrying capacity is \( M = 400 \), not \( 0.0005 \) or \( 0.2 \)!
  • Euler Concavity Error Analysis: Free-response questions frequently ask whether Euler's method overestimates or underestimates the true solution \( y(b) \):
    • If \( y''(x) > 0 \) (concave up), tangent lines lie below the curve \( \Rightarrow \) Euler's method underestimates.
    • If \( y''(x) < 0 \) (concave down), tangent lines lie above the curve \( \Rightarrow \) Euler's method overestimates.
  • Never Combine Steps in Euler's Method: Always calculate the slope \( f(x_n, y_n) \) and step explicitly: \( y_{n+1} = y_n + \Delta x \cdot f(x_n, y_n) \). AP readers require evidence of step-by-step arithmetic.
For \( \dfrac{dy}{dx}=y,\ y(0)=1 \), take one Euler step with \( h=0.5 \). \[ y(0.5)\approx 1+0.5\cdot 1=1.5. \]

question.en: The logistic model \(\dfrac{dP}{dt}=0.4P\!\left(1-\dfrac{P}{500}\right)\) has \(P(0)=50\). What is \(\lim_{t\to\infty}P(t)\)? For what \(P\) is the growth rate greatest?

solution.en: Carrying capacity \(K=500\). \(\lim P=500\). Maximum growth rate at \(P=K/2=250\).

question.en: Let \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x - y\) with initial condition \(y(0) = 2\). Use Euler's method with two steps of equal size \(h = 0.5\) to approximate \(y(1)\).
